subject: Post-call recap & follow-ups — deployment mode decision + dedicated sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Priya Nair <priya@magnohealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap & follow-ups — deployment mode decision + dedicated sizing clarifications

Hi Priya — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and the few clarifying items we promised to follow up on. I’ve also cc’d Lauren (solutions) and Ben (pricing) so we can move to a recommended pilot configuration and a procurement-friendly proposal.

Recap (high level)
- Current opt-in: evaluating Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on‑prem. Primary constraints: HIPAA-adjacent data controls and a procurement timeline that targets a signed PO by end of Q1.
- Workload shape: short latencies for chat and structured extraction. You indicated a spike-prone traffic pattern (daily peaks) and some long-run batch jobs overnight.

Numbers you gave (confirm please)
- Peak TPS (inbound requests): ~120 TPS sustained during day, with short bursts up to ~250 TPS for <2 minutes.
- Average tokens per request: ~150 tokens (prompt + response).
- Daily token volume: roughly 5M tokens/day.
- Concurrency target: ~40 concurrent sessions for interactive chat; 60+ concurrent for short batch windows.

Primary trade-offs we want to validate
1) Deployment mode: you said compliance leans toward VPC/private control, but procurement prefers the lower friction Hosted/Dedicated flow if we can meet their KMS/audit needs. If MagnoHealth requires customer‑managed KMS and full control of network egress, that pushes us to Private (VPC). Dedicated can meet most SLAs while keeping data isolated within a Redwood tenant — can you confirm which of these is a hard requirement vs nice‑to‑have?
2) GPU family: for the workload you described we typically recommend: H100s for lowest latency and larger KV cache headroom; A100 or H100 multi-instance as a cost/latency compromise; L4/NX GPUs when throughput is the only driver and latency is less critical. We’ll propose a pilot config below.
3) Token mix & bottlenecks: based on your comment about long batch jobs, please confirm the % of requests that are >512 tokens vs <64 tokens. Helps us size KV cache and batch-windowing.

Immediate proposed pilot (for discussion)
- Purpose: validate latency SLOs and cost per 1M tokens given your burst profile.
- Suggested pilot pool: 2x H100 (reserved for pilot), or 4x A100 depending on budget. Config will be backed by capacity autoscale for short bursts.
- Target pilot window: 2 weeks of production‑like traffic replay + live routing for 10% of traffic.

Action items (please reply inline)
- Priya: confirm the three numeric items above (peak TPS, avg tokens, token distribution) and whether customer‑managed KMS is required. If procurement wants a candidate contract language for data residency/KMS, we can draft an annex.
- Lauren / Ben: I’d like an initial cost/throughput estimate for both the 2x H100 and the 4x A100 pilot options. Ben — attaching the pricing draft for your reference.

Attachments: magnohealth_token_profile.csv (empty template — please fill the token distribution column); redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf (pricing assumptions).

Thanks — Marcus

Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (555) 212-0199

From: Priya Nair <priya@magnohealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@magnohealth.com
Date: 2026-12-21T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & follow-ups — deployment mode decision + dedicated sizing clarifications

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming numbers and a couple of clarifications below. Forwarding to procurement for timeline context.

Confirmations
- Peak TPS: confirmed ~120 TPS sustained, bursts to 250 TPS are accurate but typically <90s.
- Avg tokens/request: 150 tokens is correct (we sampled 500 requests after the call).
- Token distribution (rough): 70% <= 64 tokens, 25% 65–512 tokens, 5% >512 tokens (these are ballpark; attaching a CSV with more samples).

Security / deployment mode notes
- Our security team prefers customer‑managed KMS and VPC peering; that makes Private (VPC/on‑prem) the default from a compliance standpoint. Two caveats:
  1) If Redwood offers a Dedicated deployment in our AWS tenant with customer‑managed keys and audit logs we could consider that as an acceptable compromise.
  2) Procurement will prefer Dedicated/Hosted if the time to a working pilot and contract simplicity is materially faster — their goal is to start a pilot before the procurement freeze in late Q1.

Procurement timeline
- We can accept a pilot SOW signed by the end of Q1. Procurement prefers a short SOW (pilot period, acceptance criteria, and termination clause).

Next steps we want from Redwood
- Short comparison that shows: Dedicated (Redwood-managed infra but tenant isolated + optional CMK) vs Private VPC (Redwood control plane + customer infra) with callouts for KMS, audit logs, and expected lead time to pilot.
- Pilot config recommendation (H100 vs A100) with expected p50/p95 latencies and cost per 1M tokens for both.

Thanks — Priya

Priya Nair
Head of Platform, MagnoHealth
priya@magnohealth.com | +1 (415) 555-8430

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & follow-ups — deployment mode decision + dedicated sizing clarifications

Thanks Priya — that token split is super helpful. Quick replies inline and proposed next milestones.

- CMK/KMS: we can support customer-managed keys for Dedicated when the deployment runs in the customer’s cloud account (our Private offering has the most control). I’ll ask solutions to draft a short one‑page comparison (Dedicated with CMK vs Private VPC) focused on lead time and controls.
- Pilot config: given your burst profile and the token mix, our recommendation for the pilot is: 2x H100 for lowest p95 latency and KV cache headroom OR 3x A100 for a cost-balanced option. We expect p50/p95 for H100 to be ~18ms/90ms on your 150-token average workload (approx) and for A100 ~28ms/140ms — we’ll validate these in the pilot. Ben — can you prepare a 2-option SOW + cost delta for the proposed pilot?

Proposed milestones
1) Solutions note (Dedicated vs Private one-pager) — deliver by EOD Thu 12/23.
2) Pilot SOW (2x H100 and 3x A100 options) — Ben to share by Tue 12/28.
3) Technical kickoff workshop (1.5 hours) to run through VPC/KMS options and traffic replay plan — propose week of Jan 5.

Priya — does the week of Jan 5 work for the technical kickoff? If yes, what are two 90‑minute slots that work for your engineering + security folks?

—Marcus

Marcus / Ben — internal note to capture what I’ll include in the one‑pager and to align on who owns what.

Checklist for one‑pager (Dedicated w/ CMK vs Private VPC)
- KMS: exact flows for CMK (customer owns key in their account) vs Redwood-managed key — include encryption-at-rest, transit, and token redaction notes.
- Audit logs: what audit surfaces we provide for Dedicated vs Private (CloudTrail, internal audit webhook deliverables).
- Lead time: estimated calendar days for pilot spin-up: Dedicated with CMK in customer AWS account ~7–10 days (SRE onboarding + IAM), Private VPC (customer infra) ~14–21 days (network & infra procurement).
- Cost delta: high-level expected monthly committed cost ranges for 2x H100 and 3x A100 pilot pools.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency target <= 150ms on 150-token average; cache hit rate goal 85%+ for prompt prefixes.

Ben — can you draft the pilot SOW skeleton and the pricing delta (2x H100 vs 3x A100) — include expected token cost per 1M tokens and an option for a 30% burst buffer?
Marcus — I’ll draft the one‑pager and share a first pass by Thu 12/23 EOD.

—Lauren
